correctness.rationale: The tangent Taylor coefficients are strictly positive by an exact recursion from tan derivative 1+tan squared, so |z-tan z|<=tan|z|-|z|, with equality exactly for real z at nonzero modulus below pi/2. Unique R solves tan R=2R. The increasing scalar envelope maps [0,R] into itself, and real ±r saturate every iterate. For r<R its iterates decay to zero with a valid cubic quantitative bound. The two real boundary points form a repelling two-cycle; every other critical-circle point strictly enters the convergence disk and lies in its immediate component. Translation by k*pi completes the statement. Finite checker tests confirm formulas but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2024 same-map complex-dynamics article explicitly leaves its displayed centered complex convergence disk as a numerical observation. Establishing the exact sharp radius, the complete first-contact set on the critical circle, and exact worst-case modulus at every iteration is a motivated resolution of that gap and supplies rigorous uniform convergence guarantees for complex initial guesses. It is not an arbitrary parameter slice, a real-only restatement, or an unmotivated numeric bound; its proof is elementary but its object and invariant are natural and it answers a specifically published open numerical observation.
